an5.100:4.1: “Sir, the Koliyan named Kakudha—my supporter—has recently passed away and been reborn in a certain host of mind-made gods.
an5.100:4.2: His incarnation was two or three times the size of a Magadhan village with its fields.
an5.100:4.3: But with that incarnation he didn’t obstruct himself or others.
an5.100:4.4: Then, sir, the godling Kakudha came up to me, bowed, stood to one side, and said to me:
an5.100:4.5: ‘Sir, this fixed desire arose in Devadatta—
an5.100:4.6: I shall lead the mendicant Saṅgha.
an5.100:4.7: And as that thought arose, Devadatta lost that psychic power.’
an5.100:4.8: That is what the godling Kakudha said, sir.
an5.100:4.9: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right, before vanishing right there.”
an5.100:5.4: ‘Everything the godling Kakudha says is correct and not otherwise.’”
an5.100:12.2: living comfortably, the unshakable as fifth;
an5.100:12.4: the lion, and Kakudha the tenth.
